title: Titus Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Titus 3: subjection to rulers, what we once were, the washing of regeneration, the factious man, and the closing travel plans.

questions.text: What are they reminded to be ready for, along with being in subjection to rulers?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says to remind them to be in subjection to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, and to be ready for every good work.

questions.text: What does verse 2 say about how to speak of other people?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, and to show all humility toward all men.

answers.text: To speak sharply to the proud
To speak evil of no one

questions.text: How does verse 3 describe what we ourselves once were?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that we were also once foolish, disobedient and deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy.
Verse 4 says that the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared.

answers.text: The kindness of God our Savior

questions.text: According to what did he save us, since it was not by works of righteousness we did ourselves?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says that he saved us not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit.

questions.text: Through whom was the Holy Spirit poured out on us richly?
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 say that he renewed us by the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior.

questions.text: Being justified by his grace, what were we to be made heirs according to?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

questions.text: What does verse 9 say should be shunned as unprofitable and vain?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says to shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife and disputes about the law, because they are unprofitable and vain.

questions.text: What is to be done with a factious man after a first and second warning?
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 say to avoid a factious man after a first and second warning, knowing that such a one is perverted, sins, and is self-condemned.

answers.text: He is to be taught again
He is to be sent away
He is to be kept silent

questions.text: To which city is Titus asked to come, where the writer had determined to winter?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that when Artemas or Tychicus is sent, Titus should be diligent to come to him at Nicopolis, where he had determined to winter.
